card.name: "May" before a severe outcome
card.fires_on: The word "may" (or "can be") right after a warned-about condition, where it introduces a serious outcome such as ending fatally or occurring after stopping a drug. Mostly in warning sections.

modes.label: Colitis warning
modes.description: "may" after "severe colitis which" in the clindamycin or lincomycin warning, before "end fatally".
modes.example: Because clindamycin therapy has been associated with severe colitis which<< may>> end fatally, it should be reserved for

modes.label: Hepatitis B flare
modes.description: "may" after "and" in the warning about stopping emtricitabine or tenofovir products, before "occur with discontinuation".
modes.example: discontinued products containing emtricitabine (FTC) and/or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF), and<< may>> occur with discontinuation of DESCOV

modes.label: Short warning headline
modes.description: "May" or "Can be" after a colon in a bulleted warning summary, before a serious result.
modes.example: Interstitial Lung Disease/Pneumonitis: Can<< be>> fatal.

card.writes: It pushes toward words naming an outcome or consequence and away from the word "effects" or "consequences" itself.
card.plain: It marks the little word "may" that leads into a serious result, like "may end fatally".
